thread:
maria: Quick sync — we need final alignment on cutover lanes (self-serve / enterprise / regulated) + SLA/docs/pricing before GA tomorrow. Who owns which lane? Any hard blockers?

sam: I'll own self-serve lane. Docs are 90% (getting examples + sample prompts). SLA target is 99.9% availability and p99 latency goals for 1k-token requests — infra ok?

jordan: infra: availability target sounds fine for the dedicated pool; p99 for 1k tokens depends on KV cache warmup. Cold-start tails are the main risk. Suggest a fast-failover to a smaller quantized model for cold nodes as a safety net.

lee: Support: runbook drafted, needs concrete play names for 'pricing-exceeded' and 'latency-regression' incidents. Also need escalation mapping to oncall pager and SRE rotation.

ana: (typo correction) — Ana: Pricing: tier definitions are ready, but burst overage pricing and reserved capacity uplift aren't finalized. Finance needs to confirm margins before we publish public wording.

maria: Good. Can we enumerate blockers and owners as actions? Also confirm monitoring panels & alerts tied to SLA and quality regressions.

jordan: Action items I can take: 1) add 'kv_warmup_miss' metric to infra dashboard (owner: jordan) 2) add latency SLA panel and alert (owner: infra-observability) 3) wire synthetic prompt set to quality checks (owner: sam). I'll create dashboards in Grafana and link them in the runbook.

sam: I'll upload the prompt set to the docs repo and wire it to the quality-alerts job. One question: who signs off on the public pricing language and the 'subject to change' clause?

ana: Finance (cc @finance) needs final numbers; I'll draft the margin callout and a short paragraph for 'reserved vs burst' and share in #pricing-review. If finance misses EOD, we default to current phrasing with a clear 'subject to change' note.

lee: Oncall mapping: enterprise customers should map to 'enterprise-escalation' queue. Need list of pilot customers + contact handles to populate the playbook. @maria can you share?

maria: Sending the pilot list in DM now. Decision note: GA will be self-serve only. Enterprise and regulated lanes are invite-only beta for now — we need explicit language in docs and on the product page.

sam: Ack. That reduces immediate SLA obligations. Confirm rollback plan: if latency > SLA for 10m, autopause burst routing and route new requests to fallback compact model?

jordan: I'll implement automated fallback: if p95 > 400ms sustained for 5m or p99 > 1.2s for 3m, circuit-breaker routes to model-x-compact and triggers an alert. I'll add a 'fallback-engaged' metric.

infra-bot: deploy check: ded-pool-01 autoscale config validated; planned canary rollout scheduled at 1769999999 — will post status. :white_check_mark:

maria: Timeline check — docs + pricing wording by EOD, monitoring + runbooks by 06:00 UTC tomorrow, infra fallbacks in canary by 12:00 UTC. Owners recap: sam/docs, ana/pricing, jordan/infra, lee/support.

ana: Noted. Finance check expected by 18:00 PT. If they don't confirm, we ship with default pricing copy and add a bold 'subject to change' note anchored in the billing FAQ.

lee: I'll finish runbook play names and oncall mapping tonight. Quick Q: do we need an SLA credit table for self-serve GA? If so, who writes it — product or legal?

maria: Yes, include a simple credits table (availability tiers + credit percentages). Product to draft, legal to approve. Loop @legal-ops for signoff.

sam: I'll drop a PR with docs + prompt examples and put the credit table placeholder. Tagging @maria for review.

maria: Thanks everyone. If there are no major blockers by EOD, proceed with self-serve GA tomorrow. :rocket:

(threads like this are intentionally concise — we'll paste checklists into the docs repo and assign GH issues for tracking)
